label: lem:strongly_measurable_interior
title: Strong measurability at interior points
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b = [\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, and let $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$. Then $f$ is strongly measurable at the full neighborhood filter of $x$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure (i.e.\ $\texttt{StronglyMeasurableAtFilter}\; f\; (\mathcal{N}(x))\; \texttt{volume}$, where $\mathcal{N}(x) = \texttt{nhds}\; x$). This follows because $x$ belongs to the open set $\mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$, and any function continuous on an open set is strongly measurable at each point's neighborhood filter (via \texttt{ContinuousOn.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter}).
proof: Since $x$ lies in the open set $\mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$, and $f$ is continuous on the open interior (by restriction from the closed interval), we apply \texttt{ContinuousOn.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter} with \texttt{isOpen\_Ioo} to obtain $\texttt{StronglyMeasurableAtFilter}\; f\; (\texttt{nhds}\; x)\; \texttt{volume}$.
